symptom: PC0 cannot reach remote host 192.168.20.10
initial_evidence: PC0: ipconfig shows IPv4 address 192.168.10.10 with an incorrect default gateway | Router0: show ip interface brief shows 192.168.10.1 as the active router interface for the 192.168.10.0/24 network
expected_fault: Incorrect default gateway
expected_fix: Set PC0 default gateway to 192.168.10.1

symptom: PC0 cannot communicate with PC1
initial_evidence: PC0 ping to 192.168.10.11 shows 100% packet loss | Switch0: show vlan brief shows Fa0/1 in VLAN 10 and Fa0/2 in VLAN 20 | Switch0: show mac address-table learns PC0 on Fa0/1 in VLAN 10
expected_fault: PC1 switch port Fa0/2 is assigned to the wrong VLAN (VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10)
expected_fix: Assign Fa0/2 to VLAN 10 using: interface fa0/2; switchport access vlan 10

symptom: PC0 can reach its gateway but cannot ping Server0 at 192.168.20.10
initial_evidence: PC0 ping to 192.168.20.10 returns Destination host unreachable from 192.168.10.1 | PC0 ping to 192.168.10.1 succeeds | Router0: show ip route shows 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24 directly connected | Router0: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 and GigabitEthernet0/1 up/up
additional_evidence: Extended IP access list 101: 10 deny icmp host 192.168.10.10 host 192.168.20.10 (4 match(es)) | 20 permit ip any any (4 match(es))
expected_fault: ACL 101 denies ICMP traffic from PC0 (192.168.10.10) to Server0 (192.168.20.10)
expected_fix: Remove or modify the deny rule in ACL 101 to permit the intended ICMP traffic

symptom: PC2 cannot reach any network resources, not even devices in its own subnet
initial_evidence: PC2: ipconfig shows IPv4 address 192.168.30.15, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 10.0.0.1 | Router1: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 as 192.168.30.1, status up/up, for the 192.168.30.0/24 network
expected_fault: PC2's default gateway 10.0.0.1 is outside the local subnet 192.168.30.0/24
expected_fix: Set PC2 default gateway to 192.168.30.1

symptom: PC3 can ping devices on its own subnet but cannot reach the 192.168.40.0/24 server subnet
initial_evidence: PC3: ipconfig shows IPv4 address 192.168.50.20, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, default gateway 192.168.50.2 | PC3 ping to 192.168.50.2 succeeds | PC3 ping to 192.168.40.10 fails with Request timed out
additional_evidence: Router2: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.50.1 up/up and GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.40.1 up/up
expected_fault: PC3's default gateway 192.168.50.2 does not match the router's actual interface address 192.168.50.1 on that subnet
expected_fix: Set PC3 default gateway to 192.168.50.1

symptom: PC4 can reach the internet but PC5 on the same switch cannot
initial_evidence: PC4: ipconfig shows IPv4 address 192.168.60.10, default gateway 192.168.60.1 | PC5: ipconfig shows IPv4 address 192.168.60.11, default gateway 192.168.60.10 | Router3: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.60.1 up/up for the 192.168.60.0/24 network
expected_fault: PC5's default gateway 192.168.60.10 is set to a host address instead of the router interface 192.168.60.1
expected_fix: Set PC5 default gateway to 192.168.60.1

symptom: PCs connected in VLAN 1 (management) on Switch1 cannot reach VLAN 1 devices on Switch2 across the trunk, even though PCs in VLAN 10, 20, and 30 communicate normally across the same trunk link
initial_evidence: PC-Mgmt0 (Switch1, VLAN 1) ping to PC-Mgmt1 (Switch2, VLAN 1) at 192.168.1.11 times out | A PC in VLAN 10 on Switch1 successfully pings its VLAN 10 peer on Switch2 across the same trunk | Switch1: show interfaces trunk shows Gi0/1 trunking, native vlan 1, allowed vlans 1,10,20,30
additional_evidence: Switch2: show interfaces trunk shows Gi0/1 trunking, native vlan 99, allowed vlans 1,10,20,30
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch: Switch1's trunk uses native VLAN 1 while Switch2's trunk uses native VLAN 99, so untagged VLAN 1 traffic sent by Switch1 arrives on Switch2 already associated with VLAN 99; explicitly tagged VLANs (10, 20, 30) are unaffected
expected_fix: Set matching native VLANs on both ends of the trunk, e.g. on Switch2: interface gi0/1; switchport trunk native vlan 1

symptom: Clients in VLAN 10 cannot reach Server1 which should also be in VLAN 10
initial_evidence: Server1 ping to gateway 192.168.10.1 fails | Switch4: show vlan brief shows Fa0/10 (Server1 port) in VLAN 40 | Switch4: show running-config interface fa0/10 shows switchport access vlan 40
expected_fault: Server1's switch port Fa0/10 is assigned to VLAN 40 instead of VLAN 10
expected_fix: Assign Fa0/10 to VLAN 10 using: interface fa0/10; switchport access vlan 10

symptom: PC6 in VLAN 20 on Switch5 cannot reach PC7 in VLAN 20 on Switch6
initial_evidence: PC6 ping to PC7 (192.168.20.12) times out | Switch5: show interfaces trunk shows Gi0/2 trunking, allowed vlans 1,10,20 | Switch6: show interfaces trunk shows Gi0/2 trunking, allowed vlans 1,10
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is not included in the allowed VLAN list on Switch6's trunk interface Gi0/2
expected_fix: Add VLAN 20 to the allowed list on Switch6 Gi0/2 using: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20

symptom: PCs in the 192.168.70.0/24 subnet are not receiving IP addresses from DHCP
initial_evidence: PC8: ipconfig shows Autoconfiguration IP address 169.254.x.x | Router4: show ip dhcp pool shows pool LAN_POOL exists with default-router 192.168.70.1
additional_evidence: ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL network 192.168.80.0 255.255.255.0 default-router 192.168.70.1
expected_fault: The DHCP pool LAN_POOL network statement (192.168.80.0/24) does not match the actual client subnet (192.168.70.0/24)
expected_fix: Correct the pool network statement: network 192.168.70.0 255.255.255.0

symptom: No PCs in VLAN 10 can obtain a DHCP address
initial_evidence: PC9: ipconfig shows no IP address assigned | Router5: show running-config shows ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.254 and ip dhcp pool VLAN10_POOL network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: The excluded address range 192.168.10.1 to 192.168.10.254 covers the entire usable address space of the DHCP pool
expected_fix: Remove the original full-range exclusion and add a smaller one: no ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.254 then ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10

symptom: PC10 receives an IP address automatically but cannot reach any remote network
initial_evidence: PC10: ipconfig /all shows IPv4 address 192.168.90.50, default gateway 192.168.99.1 | Router6: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.90.1 up/up for the 192.168.90.0/24 network | Router6: show run shows ip dhcp pool POOL90 network 192.168.90.0 255.255.255.0 default-router 192.168.99.1
expected_fault: The DHCP pool default-router value 192.168.99.1 does not match the router's actual interface address 192.168.90.1
expected_fix: Correct the default-router statement: default-router 192.168.90.1

symptom: Some new PCs on the 192.168.100.0/29 subnet fail to receive an IP address while existing PCs keep working
initial_evidence: PC11: ipconfig shows no IP address assigned | Router7: show ip dhcp pool shows pool SMALL_POOL, Total addresses 6, Leased addresses 6, Pending event none | Router7: show ip dhcp binding lists 6 active bindings
expected_fault: The DHCP pool SMALL_POOL has exhausted its available address range (6 of 6 leased) due to an undersized subnet
expected_fix: Expand the DHCP scope, e.g. move to a /27 subnet and update the ip dhcp pool network statement accordingly

symptom: PC12 can ping IP addresses but cannot browse to websites by name
initial_evidence: PC12: ipconfig /all shows DNS server 8.8.4.8 | PC12 ping to 192.168.110.1 succeeds | PC12 nslookup www.example.com fails with Request timed out
expected_fault: PC12 is configured with an unreachable/incorrect DNS server address 8.8.4.8
expected_fix: Configure PC12 with the correct DNS server address, e.g. 192.168.110.5

symptom: All PCs in the office cannot resolve hostnames even though the DNS server address is configured correctly
initial_evidence: PC13: ipconfig /all shows DNS server 192.168.120.5, matching network documentation | PC13 nslookup www.example.com fails | PC13 ping to 192.168.120.5 fails with Request timed out
additional_evidence: Switch7: show interfaces status shows Fa0/8 (connected to DNS Server0) in a notconnect state, disabled
expected_fault: The DNS server at 192.168.120.5 is unreachable because its switch port Fa0/8 is down
expected_fix: Restore connectivity to the DNS server, e.g. reconnect the cable or issue no shutdown on Fa0/8

symptom: PC14 can ping www.internal.local by IP but browsing to the hostname loads the wrong server
initial_evidence: PC14 ping to 192.168.130.10 (intended web server) succeeds | PC14 nslookup www.internal.local resolves to 192.168.130.20
additional_evidence: Router8 running-config shows ip host www.internal.local 192.168.130.20
expected_fault: The router's local IOS host-table entry (ip host) for www.internal.local points to 192.168.130.20 instead of the intended 192.168.130.10
expected_fix: Correct the host entry: no ip host www.internal.local 192.168.130.20 then ip host www.internal.local 192.168.130.10

symptom: PC15 on the 192.168.140.0/24 network cannot reach Server2 on the remote 192.168.150.0/24 network
initial_evidence: PC15 ping to Server2 192.168.150.10 fails with Destination host unreachable from 192.168.140.1 | Router9: show ip route shows only 192.168.140.0/24 and 192.168.160.0/30 as connected routes, no entry for 192.168.150.0/24
expected_fault: Router9 has no route to the 192.168.150.0/24 network

symptom: PC16 cannot reach the 192.168.170.0/24 remote network despite a route being present
initial_evidence: PC16 ping to 192.168.170.10 fails | Router10: show ip route shows S 192.168.170.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.160.10 | Router10: show ip interface brief shows the WAN link Serial0/0/0 as 192.168.160.1 up/up, connected to neighbor 192.168.160.6
expected_fault: The static route next hop 192.168.160.10 does not match the actual neighbor router address 192.168.160.6

symptom: Router12 can ping directly connected networks but the remote branch network 192.168.190.0/24 is missing from all routers' routing tables
initial_evidence: Router11 (branch): show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.190.1 up/up | Router12 (HQ): show ip route shows no entry for 192.168.190.0/24, only local and other OSPF routes
additional_evidence: Router11 running-config shows router ospf 1 network 192.168.191.0 0.0.0.255 area 0, with no network statement covering 192.168.190.0/24
expected_fault: Router11's OSPF configuration lacks a network statement for the 192.168.190.0/24 interface, so it is never advertised
expected_fix: Add the missing network statement: network 192.168.190.0 0.0.0.255 area 0

symptom: Traffic from PC17 to the 192.168.200.0/24 server network fails to reach its destination
initial_evidence: PC17 ping to 192.168.200.10 fails | Router13: show ip route shows S 192.168.200.0/24 [1/0] via 192.168.180.2 exiting Serial0/1/0 | Router13: show ip interface brief shows Serial0/1/0 down/down and Serial0/0/0 up/up | Router13: show interfaces description shows Serial0/0/0 described as WAN link to Branch-B 192.168.200.0/24 and Serial0/1/0 described as Backup WAN link currently down
expected_fault: The static route for 192.168.200.0/24 points out the down Serial0/1/0 interface instead of Serial0/0/0, which the interface description identifies as the active link to that network
expected_fix: Update the static route to use the active interface: ip route 192.168.200.0 255.255.255.0 Serial0/0/0

symptom: PC18 can ping Server3 but cannot open its web page
initial_evidence: PC18 ping to Server3 192.168.210.10 succeeds | PC18 browser request to http://192.168.210.10 times out | Router14: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/1 up/up facing Server3's subnet
additional_evidence: Extended IP access list 110: 10 deny tcp any host 192.168.210.10 eq 80 (12 match(es)) | 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL 110 denies TCP port 80 (HTTP) traffic to Server3
expected_fix: Modify ACL 110 to permit HTTP traffic to 192.168.210.10 on port 80

symptom: Server4 cannot initiate connections to outside hosts even though the ACL is intended to restrict only inbound traffic
initial_evidence: Router15: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/1 as 192.168.220.1, the interface directly facing Server4's LAN segment, and GigabitEthernet0/0 facing the outside network | Router15: show running-config interface gigabitEthernet0/1 shows ip access-group 120 out | Router15: show access-lists shows access-list 120 permit tcp any host 192.168.220.10 eq 80, with all other traffic implicitly denied
expected_fault: ACL 120 is applied outbound on GigabitEthernet0/1, the interface facing Server4's own LAN. In that direction the ACL only permits inbound web traffic to 192.168.220.10, so all other traffic the router forwards toward Server4's subnet -- including return traffic for connections Server4 itself initiates outward -- is caught by the implicit deny
expected_fix: Reapply the ACL on the interface facing the outside network instead, e.g. ip access-group 120 in on GigabitEthernet0/0, or add explicit permit statements on Gi0/1 out for Server4's outbound return traffic

symptom: Admin PC19 cannot establish an SSH session to Router16 even though other subnet devices are permitted
initial_evidence: PC19 (192.168.230.20) ping to Router16 192.168.230.1 succeeds | PC19 SSH attempt to 192.168.230.1 times out | Router16: show ip interface brief shows the management interface up/up
additional_evidence: Standard IP access list 15: 10 permit 192.168.230.0 0.0.0.15 (referenced by the vty access-class)
expected_fault: ACL 15's wildcard mask 0.0.0.15 only covers addresses 192.168.230.0 to 192.168.230.15, excluding PC19 at 192.168.230.20 from the permitted vty access list
expected_fix: Correct the wildcard mask to cover the full subnet: access-list 15 permit 192.168.230.0 0.0.0.255

symptom: Only one internal host at a time can access the internet; additional hosts fail to reach external websites
initial_evidence: PC20 (192.168.240.10) can browse the internet | PC21 (192.168.240.11) ping to 8.8.8.8 fails | Router17: show ip nat translations shows a single active translation for 192.168.240.10
additional_evidence: Router17 running-config shows ip nat inside source list 1 pool NATPOOL, where NATPOOL is a dynamic address pool defined as ip nat pool NATPOOL 203.0.113.5 203.0.113.5 netmask 255.255.255.255, configured without the overload keyword
expected_fault: NAT is configured as a dynamic pool without overload (no PAT), so it maps only one internal host to the single public address at a time and cannot support multiple simultaneous translations
expected_fix: Enable PAT by adding the overload keyword: ip nat inside source list 1 pool NATPOOL overload

symptom: PCs on the 192.168.250.0/24 LAN cannot reach the internet even though address translation appears configured
initial_evidence: PC22 ping to 8.8.8.8 fails | Router18: show running-config shows access-list 1 permit 192.168.251.0 0.0.0.255 and ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload | Router18: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/1 192.168.250.1 up/up as the LAN interface
expected_fault: NAT access-list 1 references the wrong subnet 192.168.251.0/24 instead of the actual LAN subnet 192.168.250.0/24
expected_fix: Correct the ACL: no access-list 1 permit 192.168.251.0 0.0.0.255 then access-list 1 permit 192.168.250.0 0.0.0.255

symptom: No hosts on the internal LAN can reach the internet, and show ip nat translations stays empty despite traffic attempts
initial_evidence: PC23 ping to 8.8.8.8 fails | Router19: show running-config shows interface GigabitEthernet0/0 (LAN side) configured with ip nat outside, and interface GigabitEthernet0/1 (WAN side) configured with ip nat inside
expected_fault: The NAT inside and outside interface designations are reversed on Router19
expected_fix: Correct the interface roles: interface GigabitEthernet0/0; ip nat inside / interface GigabitEthernet0/1; ip nat outside

symptom: During peak hours, some internal hosts lose internet access while others continue to work fine
initial_evidence: PC24 and PC25 can browse normally | PC26 ping to 8.8.8.8 fails during peak usage | Router20: show running-config shows ip nat inside source list 1 pool NATPOOL, a dynamic pool with no overload keyword present | Router20: show ip nat statistics shows Pool NATPOOL: netmask 255.255.255.248, start 203.0.113.10 end 203.0.113.14, total addresses 5, allocated 5 (100%)
additional_evidence: Router20: show ip nat translations lists 5 active translations, each mapped one-to-one to a distinct pool address with no port-based sharing, confirming the pool is fully allocated
expected_fault: NAT pool NATPOOL is configured without overload and has only 5 addresses, exhausting available translations under peak load
expected_fix: Add the overload keyword to allow port-based address sharing: ip nat inside source list 1 pool NATPOOL overload

symptom: Laptop0 cannot see or connect to the office wireless network
initial_evidence: Laptop0: PC Wireless GUI (Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect tab) shows configured SSID OfficeNet | AP0: GUI Config tab (Interface > Wireless0 > Basic Wireless Settings) shows the broadcast SSID configured as Office_Net on VLAN 50
expected_fault: Laptop0 is configured with SSID OfficeNet which does not match the access point's actual SSID Office_Net
expected_fix: Update Laptop0's wireless profile SSID to Office_Net

symptom: Laptop1 detects the correct SSID but repeatedly fails to associate with the wireless network
initial_evidence: Laptop1: PC Wireless settings shows SSID HomeNet matching AP1's broadcast SSID, authentication WPA2-PSK with passphrase wireless123 | AP1: show running-config wlan shows WPA2-PSK passphrase configured as Wireless2024
expected_fault: Laptop1's configured WPA2 passphrase does not match the access point's configured passphrase
expected_fix: Update Laptop1's wireless passphrase to match the AP: Wireless2024

symptom: Wireless clients associate successfully and get an IP address, but cannot reach internal servers that wired VLAN 10 clients can reach
initial_evidence: Laptop2 associates to AP2 with strong signal and obtains IP 192.168.60.150 | Laptop2 ping to internal Server5 192.168.10.50 fails | AP2 is connected to Switch8 port Fa0/15
additional_evidence: Switch8: show vlan brief shows Fa0/15 assigned to VLAN 60, while wireless clients are expected to be on VLAN 10 with Server5
expected_fault: AP2's switch port Fa0/15 is assigned to VLAN 60 instead of the intended wireless VLAN 10, placing wireless clients on the wrong subnet
expected_fix: Reassign Fa0/15 to VLAN 10: interface fa0/15; switchport access vlan 10
